batch.title: Forest restoration: findings that move a rating (first check)
batch.notes: Every forest restoration finding that no person has checked yet and that would change a rating if it were wrong. Each card says what the paper says, what we recorded and what looks wrong (or that it checks out), and what Approve or Reject would change today (trial run, 10 Nov). The AI's suggested call shows under the buttons; it is a suggestion only. Approve = recorded correctly, stays in use. Hold = leave it open with a note. Reject = set aside (kept on record, no longer counted); pick a reason.

units.citation: Porto et al. (2009). Investigating the effects of afforestation on soil erosion and sediment mobilisation in two small catchments in Southern Italy. CATENA.
units.quote: For all events, the sediment concentrations listed for plot P1 are substantially greater than those from plot 2. This difference further conﬁrms the increased erosion rates associated with areas with little or no tree cover in catchment W2, as represented by plot P1, and therefore the importance of the forest canopy in reducing erosion.

relationship.outcome_raw: sediment concentration in runoff, sparse/no tree cover plot vs good-cover plot in eucalyptus afforestation

context.note: eucalyptus afforestation (1968) of former rangeland; plots P1 vs P2, 10 events; process: family re-homed active_planting -> plantation 2026-10-19 (Pete ruling 4, plantation split; audit pipeline/staging/plantation_audit/worklist.csv)

units.question: Porto 2009 (Italy) found far more sediment in runoff from a bare patch than from a well-covered patch inside a eucalyptus planting, and credits the tree canopy with cutting erosion. We recorded it as plantations lowering erosion. Looks right, though both patches sit inside the planting, so it shows cover matters rather than planting versus no planting. Approve keeps it. Reject: erosion for plantations stays 'conflicting evidence' but confidence falls from medium to low. AI's view: Direction and wording match the quote; the within-planting comparison is a minor caveat.

units.citation: Badji et al. (2013). Effet de l’âge de la mise en défens sur la reconstitution de la végétation ligneuse des espaces sylvo pastoraux du sud bassin arachidier (Sénégal). Journal of Applied Biosciences.
units.quote: Il varie de 27 espèces dans la mise en défens de 1 an à 51 espèces dans les mises en défens de 5 et 12 ans. Ce qui montre que la richesse spécifique est plus élevée dans les mises en défens plus âgées et a permis d’augmenter plus de 52% la richesse spécifique. (English: It ranges from 27 species in the 1-year exclosure to 51 species in the 5- and 12-year exclosures. This shows that species richness is higher in older exclosures and increased species richness by more than 52%.)

relationship.outcome_raw: woody species richness in 5- and 12-year exclosures vs 1-year exclosure

context.note: chronosequence (space-for-time) of village silvopastoral exclosures (mise en defens) aged 1, 5 and 12 years; 127 plots of 900 m2; passive regeneration of woody savanna vegetation by protection from cutting

units.question: Badji 2013 (Senegal) counted 51 woody species in village plots protected from cutting for 5 and 12 years, against 27 in a plot protected for 1 year. We recorded a strong gain in biodiversity from natural regrowth. Looks right; the 1-year plot stands in for unprotected land. Approve keeps it. Reject: the separate upper-middle-income biodiversity line for forest restoration (moderate gain, very high confidence, 7 papers) would no longer show, as it would then match the overall rating. AI's view: Numbers and direction are in the quote; young plot is a fair baseline.

units.question: Barajas-Guzmán 2013 (Mexico) found each surviving seedling cost US$2.45 with plastic mulch versus US$18 on bare soil. We recorded this as tree planting reducing cost. But the comparison is mulch versus no mulch inside a planting, not the cost of planting itself. Approve keeps it as stated. Reject: the cost row for active planting disappears, the one for natural regrowth also disappears, and the whole-practice cost row drops from high to medium confidence. AI's view: The contrast is a mulching technique within planting, not the practice's own cost.

units.citation: Brancalion et al. (2019). What makes ecosystem restoration expensive? A systematic cost assessment of projects in Brazil. Biological Conservation.
units.quote:
Direct seeding and seedling
planting cost approximately ten times more (∼US$2000. ha−1) than
less intensive restoration approaches (natural and assisted regenera-
tion, and enrichment planting; ∼US$200. ha−1), mostly due to the
higher input costs

relationship.outcome_raw: approximate total restoration cost per hectare of direct seeding and seedling planting

context.practice_as_described: 'direct seeding and seedling planting' of native species throughout the site, with site preparation, fencing/firebreaks and weed control; heavy use of machinery, fertilisers and herbicides
context.note: practitioner surveys (40 cost responses) plus 27 budget worksheets, Atlantic Forest / Amazon / Cerrado; December 2018 US$ (IGP-DI deflated); cost = implementation + maintenance; 'The vast majority of costs were incurred during the implementation phase for all methods, except for assisted regeneration, in which total restoration costs were divided evenly between implementation and maintenance', and nearly 80% of projects ended maintenance within 30 months - so the money buys ESTABLISHMENT (early maintenance is part of establishing); excludes land opportunity cost and long-term maintenance (authors: 'certainly underestimate'). Table 1 mean seedling planting cost is higher (table cell not used).

units.question: Brancalion 2019 (Brazil) says direct seeding and seedling planting cost about US$2,000 per hectare, ten times the cheaper methods. We recorded this as the cost of planting. Looks right. Approve keeps it. Reject: the planting cost row stays unrated but confidence falls from high to medium (5 to 4 papers); the separate upper-middle-income cost line would stop standing apart, and one for low- and lower-middle-income countries would show instead. AI's view: Figure and practice are both in the quote.

plain.direction_reads: ↑ higher cost · harm of the practice

plain.described: The source describes what was done as: “'direct seeding and seedling planting' of native species throughout the site, with site preparation, fencing/firebreaks and weed control; heavy use of machinery, fertilisers and herbicides”.

band.value: an absolute value of 2000 usd per ha
band.rule: |value| ≥ 1000
band.basis: ORDINAL cost class — 'is this a big or small amount given the context' (Pete 2026-10-05; no currency/price-year normalisation). Thresholds are scoping-grade, set against a typical LMIC smallholder gross margin of roughly USD 200–800/ha/yr; UMIC thresholds ×2, HIC ×5. slight = small · moderate · strong = large. Adjust the thresholds, not the mechanism.

context.practice_as_described: assisted regeneration, where 'weed control was the predominant cost' and costs were 'divided evenly between implementation and maintenance'
context.note: practitioner surveys (40 cost responses) plus 27 budget worksheets, Atlantic Forest / Amazon / Cerrado; December 2018 US$ (IGP-DI deflated); cost = implementation + maintenance; 'The vast majority of costs were incurred during the implementation phase for all methods, except for assisted regeneration, in which total restoration costs were divided evenly between implementation and maintenance', and nearly 80% of projects ended maintenance within 30 months - so the money buys ESTABLISHMENT (early maintenance is part of establishing); excludes land opportunity cost and long-term maintenance (authors: 'certainly underestimate'). the ~200 figure is stated for natural + assisted regeneration + enrichment planting together. Half the assisted-regeneration cost is maintenance (weed control during establishment) - still establishment by what the money buys.

units.question: Brancalion 2019 (Brazil) gives about US$200 per hectare for the cheaper methods, lumping assisted regrowth with natural regrowth and enrichment planting. Reject: the assisted-regrowth cost row drops from high to medium confidence (4 papers to 3); the separate upper-middle-income cost line would no longer show, as it would then match the overall rating. AI's view: Pooled figure is acceptable for a rough big-or-small cost reading.

relationship.outcome_raw: forest-fire incidence / occurrence inside protected areas vs comparable unprotected land (pooled Hedges' g, coded so positive = fewer fires); 95% CI 0.23 to 0.41 excludes zero; N = 4 estimates, I2 0%

context.practice_as_described: Protected areas (PAs): legal designation and management of existing natural forest and other natural land as protected areas, pooled by the review with a small number of payments-for-ecosystem-services (PES) / REDD+ evaluations (the review groups 'protected areas (including PES)', p26). No planting or restoration: the practice is keeping existing forest standing. BASELINE (comparator): comparable unprotected land with no intervention ('No intervention' in Table 4, pp23-25), mostly via matched controlled before-after / difference-in-differences quasi-experimental designs. Mechanism (review, p22/p26): protection restricts the clearing and burning that ignite forest fires, so fire occurrence inside the protected forest falls.
context.note: Review's OWN pooled estimate (random-effects meta-analysis of Hedges' g; outcomes transformed so a positive g is the desirable direction, i.e. g > 0 for fire = fewer fires, p22). Table 6 'Meta-analysis findings by intervention group' (p31); columns Intervention, Outcome, g, 95% CI, N (effect estimates), I2, tau2. Left out of this lane: 'Natural land cover' and 'Income' rows (single estimates, N = 1: Beresford et al. 2013 and McNally et al. 2011 -> cited originals, not units); 'Vegetation cover' row (NDVI/EVI vegetation index = proxy, no VONT id; ontology hold); land-tenure, public-audit and early-warning rows (not NbS). Included PA studies are mostly Latin America (Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Mexico, Peru) plus Indonesia, Madagascar, Tanzania and multi-LMIC panels; income_group set to upper_middle (the dominant group), not upgraded. Review reports funnel-plot asymmetry consistent with small-study / publication bias (p28) and rates most included studies high risk of bias. The 4 estimates are Carmenta et al. 2016, Nelson & Chomitz 2011, Nolte 2014 (protected areas) and Tabor et al. 2017 (PES/REDD+), p26. Caveat stated by the review (p26): Carmenta et al. 2016 found the fire reduction inside the forest occurred alongside an INCREASE in fire in the densely populated 10 km buffer zone (leakage; not in the pooled estimate). Figure 15 gives the near-identical intervention-pooled value (g = 0.31; 0.22, 0.40; p22).

context.practice_as_described: forestland restoration: 'returning farmland or bare land to forests' (control = cropland or bare land); planted vs natural regeneration not distinguished
context.note: Mechanism given for the weak N response (p5): lignin-rich woody litter has low N and microbes consume soil N to decompose it.

units.question: Yang 2023 (a pooled review) found soil nitrogen 3% higher where cropland was returned to forest, with no clear difference. We recorded that correctly, but it is counted towards yields. Soil nitrogen under a new forest says little about crop yields, since the crops are gone. Approve keeps it counting. Reject: yields for mixed-method restoration move from conflicting to moderate negative, the same for upper-middle-income countries; a separate low-income yields line would show as strong positive. AI's view: The record is faithful, but using forest soil nitrogen as a sign of crop yields is doubtful and moves several yield ratings.

units.question: A WOCAT case from India (village plantations, assisted regrowth and fodder nurseries under a village forest council) rates the effect on downstream siltation +3: 'helped slow down sediment and runoff'. We recorded a strong water-quality gain under community forest protection. It is a compiler's rating, not a measurement, and it could equally sit under tree planting. Approve keeps it. Reject: the water-quality line for forest protection would show no rating. AI's view: Rating read correctly; practitioner ratings are already weighted down.
